“Dr. Waldron, Elsie needs help!” Elsie’s husband was adamant, almost angry, as he stared at me. On the other hand, Elsie stared at the floor, almost as though she wasn’t present. I had never met either of the couple before and was struggling just a little to figure out what was needed from me to help her.

“What is going on?” I asked as I flipped through her chart. This was still in the days of paper charts, and I headed to the lab section of her chart. There wasn’t anything too crazy that I could see there—her liver enzymes were a little elevated, but otherwise, everything seemed OK.

“It’s her drinking!” Her husband told me. “She is drinking more and more every night. She won’t go out except to get whiskey. She drinks till she passes out every night and has to have something every morning to get her started.”

“Is that true?” I asked Elsie, feeling like a judge overseeing a jury trial.

“Yes,” she said. Her face was emotionless, and I couldn’t tell if she wanted to be there or not.

“Do you want help?” I asked her. This was a loaded question. Many people who struggle with alcoholism aren’t ready to break free from its vice-like hold on them. Maybe Elsie was different.

“I guess so,” she said, indifferently. Once again, I couldn’t tell whether she wanted to be there or not.

“At the rate at which you are drinking, you will kill yourself within a year – maybe two at best – if you don’t give up alcohol entirely,” I told her. “If you want to, I will try to find you an inpatient program to detox you and get you off of alcohol.”

“She’s ready,” he husband said firmly.

When dealing with someone who drinks heavily, it is crucial that they don’t simply stop drinking without medical support. Abrupt cessation of alcohol use causes the body to go into withdrawal which can produce a state called Delirium Tremens and even seizures.

I stepped out of the exam room and to make phone calls. It is never easy to find a place for someone to attempt to rehabilitate from any kind of substances, and it was over an hour and a half before I found a facility that was willing to take Elsie and try to help her get off of the whiskey.

I sighed as I reentered her exam room. I had been afraid that I wouldn’t find anywhere for her to go.

I told them about the plan, and her husband nodded vigorously, while Elise continued to stare silently at the floor. “Can we pray together before you go?” I asked them, and when they nodded assent, I prayed with them, asking for freedom and Jesus’ presence in both of their lives.

They left my office with marching orders and directions on where to go. I had a happy glow about me for the rest of the morning, knowing that I had gone the extra mile and had really made a difference in this middle-aged couple’s life.

Around 2 pm, I got a call from the rehab facility. They hadn’t seen even a shadow of Elsie or her husband, which was surprising, since it was a bright sunny day and the facility wasn’t that far away. With a sinking feeling, I dialed the couple’s phone number.

“She won’t go!” Her husband told me. “She tells me that she told me this ahead of time. She’ll try to cut back, but she isn’t willing to go into a rehab facility or any such thing. I guess just tell them that we’ll let them know if she changes her mind.”

My nurse called the rehab facility and told them the bad news, and I sat down in my chair, stunned. What else could I have done? Was there a solution for Elsie—something different that I could have said that would have made a difference in her life?

About a year later, I received the sad news that Elsie had died at home. I was certain that things would have been different if she had gone to rehab and if she had given control to Jesus. None of that had happened, and I felt cynicism pushing into my heart.

Cynicism

We live in an age of cynicism. In ancient Greece, the cynics were an odd assortment of men who specialized in being grouchy and saying mean (they would have said truthful) things to people. They often dressed in rags and behaved in such a way that most of the polite Athenians did not want to be close to them.

Today, cynicism means a tendency to believe the worst about people and circumstances. Cynical people believe that all people are motivated purely by selfishness and that bad events will tend to prevail.

Many young doctors are idealistic and very hopeful. They believe that if they exert the utmost effort, they can make a real, positive impact on their patient’s lives. Unfortunately, as time goes by and they try their hardest and their patients don’t change, they can give up. These doctors still try, but they no longer really hope that their efforts will make much of a difference.

It seems as though people who get involved with politics often have the best of intentions. They see this as a path to changing society for the better. Unfortunately, as time goes by and the faces in charge change, the policies don’t really change, they tend to become cynical.

Sometimes this cynicism is directed against all politicians. Sometimes it is only anger directed against members of the party that opposes their party’s positions. Hope is replaced by cynicism.

Cynicism in the Bible

If there is a book in the Bible that seems to have been written by a cynical man, it is the book of Ecclesiastes. The Preacher, who we understand to be Solomon, lists all of the things that he endeavored in an attempt to find joy.

In chapter 2:17-23 Solomon describes work as futile. He finishes by saying, “For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he hath laboured under the sun? For all his days are sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.” (Ecclesiastes 2:22,23)

He saw the world as being dominated by tyrants and there was little that the people could do about it. Solomon went so far as to say that political power was meaningless “Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished. For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also he that is born in his kingdom becometh poor” (Ecclesiastes 4:13).

In Ecclesiastes 6:6, he seems to disparage long life. “Yea, though he live a thousand years twice told, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?”

Of course, he finishes his short book with the instruction to remember our Creator in the days of our youth. There is a blessing for those who choose to focus on God when they have a little bit of energy left and not, when they are old and jaded, like Solomon.

Later on, it almost seemed as though God had given up on His people. He still sent prophets to them, but He knew without a doubt that the people would refuse to respond. “Therefore thou shalt speak all these words unto them; but they will not hearken to thee: thou shalt also call unto them; but they will not answer thee” (Jeremiah 7:27).

Even in the New Testament, Paul told Timothy that the time was coming when people would no longer listen to sound doctrine. “For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears;” (2 Timothy 4:3).

By picking and choosing these passages, we can come away with a very gloomy view of the future and, more specifically, of human’s willingness to change. It seems there is little point of investing ourselves in the people around us. They are full of woe and are as likely to change as a chipmunk is to master differential calculus.

The Opposite of Cynicism

The opposite of cynicism is hope. It is the belief that the future could be better.

It is interesting that the Apostle Paul spoke of tribulations in the Epistle to the Romans, “And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope: and hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us” (Romans 5:3-5).

We may not have reached the place where we glory in the trials we experience, but certainly, they should bring us these other things that he mentions. For, we grow in patience and experience, even as we deal with trials, but more than that, we come to realize that we have hope for tomorrow because we serve a great God.

The contrast in the story of the Prodigal Son in Luke 15 teaches us much about hope. The father and the older brother were strikingly different in their attitudes.

The father had never given up hope – he knew that his son had failed him and gone far from what he knew was right and yet, the father still desired to see the prodigal come to himself and return home.

On the other hand, the older brother not only had no hope for his younger brother, but he was also angry with him. The prodigal had wasted his money, he had lived in sin, and now, he had returned home just because he was out of money.

Certainly, there was no reason to trust the younger son. Yet, that is exactly what our Heavenly Father does for us.

Look for Hope in the Right Places

Part of the problem is that we look for hope in the wrong places. A number of years ago, a presidential candidate ran for office under the slogan “Hope and Change,” and yet, even though he was elected, I imagine most folks did not feel that their lives were significantly changed for the better.

Pursuing the things this world values—political power and wealth is guaranteed to bring emptiness. This is Satan’s pattern—he always over-promises and under-delivers.

This was what he did when he tempted Jesus, “All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me” (Matthew 4:8). All of the things Satan offered, nothing compared with the glory that Jesus eventually received from the road that led to the cross.

In the same way, Satan would like to distract Christians from seeking the things that are valuable, and that will bring hope. Satan tells Christians that politics will not only change the world for the better, it is an easier way to change the world.

The Bible is clear that we build hope as we nurture our relationship with God and then work to help our brothers and sisters build that same relationship in their own lives. The reason that we can hope is not because people are so wonderful—we don’t have to live very long to realize that they aren’t. The reason we hope is because we serve an awesome, faithful God who walks with us through the worst of our trials.

Remember that We Have Undeserved Hope

Jesus’ messages about forgiveness make it clear that one of the major reasons that we have for forgiving others in our lives is that we have received great and undeserved forgiveness. The same is true for hope.

Each one of us was hopeless and without reason to expect to receive hope and we were still given a ray of light in the midst of our darkness. Maybe part of the reason that we have so much trouble hoping for good things for the people around us is that we do not remember how hopeless we were before we found grace.

If Jesus was able to bring hope to our hopeless existence, then certainly He can do wonderful things in the hearts and lives of others around us. The only people we should give up on are the ones that our Savior has given up on as well.

Small Efforts Do Make a Difference

I remember having a conversation with a young person who was planning to go into medicine and had a plan to go to a foreign country and serve the people there. As we were talking, an older man entered the conversation and shared that he saw little hope for change in developing countries.

The people in those countries just weren’t interested in getting better and didn’t do the minimum necessary to stave off things like worms and parasites. Doctors and nurses couldn’t make a difference in such an environment.

I could sense the heart of the youth sinking as this older man shared. He had experience, and he had given up hope. The sad thing was that he was also stealing the hope of someone who still had a desire to serve.

When I was in training, I had a surgeon tell me that family doctors didn’t really do anything. They simply kept their patients alive till their next office visit, whereas surgeons really “fixed” people—taking out (or off) the offending body part.

At the end of the day, small efforts do make a difference. I don’t do brain surgery, but I still can make a difference in someone else’s life— maybe just by spending a little time and listening and praying. This is true for all of us.

More than that, we come to realize that making this effort changes our own lives for the better. Jesus told the sheep that as they ministered to “the least of these my brethren,” they were ministering to Him.

Even if no one’s life is improved, our Savior knows our desires and feels our efforts, and will reward them someday.

A Few Things to Remember

When we face failures, we tend to move in one of two directions. Those of us who are optimists tend to believe that this episode was an isolated event and that the future is still bright. On the other hand, pessimists believe that failures are permanent, personal, and pervasive.

Pessimists believe that their failures are the result of intrinsic character flaws that they have and that these things affect all of their lives and are unlikely to change. Unlike the righteous man who falls to rise again, these people fall and lie where they fall, defeated at the outset.

When we are dealing with other people, we need to give them the same grace that we should give ourselves. They, too, are growing, and if they have a failure today, they will do better tomorrow. Maybe they will fail again, but they will at least “fail better.”

Conclusion

Cynicism is rife in our world. Many have given up hope for a better future, and it is understandable for those who have invested their hope in this world’s institutions. There is no real hope in government or in armies or in bureaucracy.

The song says, “Oh to have no hope in Jesus, how dark this world must be!” For, Jesus is the one who brings light into our darkness and allows us to continue, even when others fail us.

God is the one who redeems us. He is the one who sent the prophets, even though their messages were ignored, and the prophets were persecuted. He is the one who continues to hope for us, even when we have failed Him so many times in the past.

He is the reason we carry on. He is the reason that we have hope, not only for ourselves but also for our brothers.

“Dr. Waldron, Elsie anahitaji msaada!” Mume wa Elsie alikuwa mkali, karibu hasira, alipotazama kinywani mwangu. Kwa upande mwingine, Elsie alitazama sakafu, kana kwamba hapana kabisa. Sikuwahi kukutana na wawili hao kabla na nilikuwa nikijaribu kidogo kujua nini kilihitajika kutoka kwangu ili kumsaidia.

“Nini kinatokea?” niliuliza nikipitia kadi yake ya matibabu. Hizi zilikuwa zikiwa bado ni za karatasi, na nikaelekea sehemu ya maabara kwenye kadi yake. Hakukuwa na chochote kigumu nilichoona huko—enzimu za ini zilikuwa juu kidogo, lakini vinginevyo, kila kitu kilionekana sawa.

“Ni kunywa kwake!” Mume wake aliniambia. “Anakunywa zaidi na zaidi kila usiku. Haatoki mbali isipokuwa kupata whiskey. Anakunywa hadi atalala kila usiku na lazima awe na kitu kila asubuhi ili kuanza.”

“Je, hilo ni kweli?” niliimuuliza Elsie, nikiwa nashikilia maamuzi kwa njia ya mwamuzi mbele ya juri.

“Ndiyo,” alisema. Uso wake haukuwa na hisia, na sikuweza kusema kama alikuwa anataka kuwepo au la.

“Unataka msaada?” niliimuuliza. Hili lilikuwa swali lenye uzito. Watu wengi wanaopambana na uraibu wa pombe hawako tayari kuachana na utegemezi huo gumu. Labda Elsie alikuwa tofauti.

“Nadhani ndio,” alisema, bila kujali. Mara nyingine tena, sikuweza kusema kama alikuwa anataka kuwa hapo au la.

“Kwa kiwango unachokunywa, utajiua ndani ya mwaka—labda miaka miwili kwa nafasi—ikiwa hautaacha kabisa pombe,” nikamwambia. “Ikiwa unataka, nitajaribu kukupeleka kwenye programu ya kuingia hospitalini ili kukutuliza na kukuondoa kwenye pombe.”

“Yuko tayari,” mume wake alisema kwa uthabiti.

Wakati wa kushughulika na mtu anayekunywa kwa wingi, ni muhimu kwamba wasiache kunywa ghafla bila msaada wa matibabu. Kuacha kabisa matumizi ya pombe husababisha mwili kuingia katika dalili za kuondolewa ambazo zinaweza kusababisha hali inayoitwa Delirium Tremens na hata kufichua (seizures).

Nilitoka chumba cha ukaguzi na kwenda kupiga simu. Si rahisi kamwe kupata mahali pa mtu kujaribu kupona kutoka kwa aina yoyote ya vimeng’enya, na ilichukua zaidi ya saa moja na nusu kabla sijapata kituo kilichokuwa tayari kumchukua Elsie na kujaribu kumsaidia kuacha whiskey.

Nilisonga kwa msongo wa kupumua niliyorudi chumbani mwake wa ukaguzi. Nilikuwa nimeogopa kuwa sitapata mahali pa kumpeleka.

Niliwaambia kuhusu mpango, na mume wake alikubali kwa kusinyaa kichwa kwa nguvu, wakati Elsie aliendelea kutazama sakafu kimya. “Tunaweza kuomba pamoja kabla haujaondoka?” niliwauliza, na walipokubali, niliwaombea, nikiomba uhuru na uwepo wa Yesu maishani mwao wote wawili.

Walienda ofisini kwangu wakiwa na maagizo ya kukanyaga na mwelekeo wa wapi waenda. Nilihisi furaha asubuhi yote, nikiwa najua kwamba nilikuwa nimeweza kwenda hatua zaidi na kwa kweli nimetoa tofauti maishani mwa jamaa hao wa umri wa kati.

Kuwa karibu saa 2 asubuhi, nilipokea simu kutoka kituo cha kupona. Hawakuwa wameona hata kivuli cha Elsie au mumewe, jambo lililoshangaza, kwa kuwa ilikuwa siku yenye jua kali na kituo hakikuwa mbali sana. Kwa hisia ya kutokwa na damu, nilipiga nambari ya wawili hao.

“Haataki kwenda!” Mume wake aliniambia. “Ananiambia kwamba alinielezea hili mapema. Atajaribu kupunguza, lakini hayuko tayari kuingia kituo cha kupona au kitu kama hicho. Nadhani tu muambieni kwamba tutawajulisha ikiwa atabadilika mawazo.”

Nurse wangu alimpigia simu kituo cha kupona na kuwaambia habari mbaya, na nikaketi kiti changu, nimezembea. Ningeweza kufanya nini zaidi? Je, kulikuwa na suluhisho kwa Elsie—mambo tofauti ambayo ningesema ambayo yangefanya tofauti maishani mwake?

Kila karibu mwaka baadaye, nilipokea habari za kusikitisha kwamba Elsie alikufa nyumbani. Nilikuwa nina uhakika mambo yangekuwa tofauti angeenda kupona na angeweka mamlaka kwa Yesu. Hakukuwa na chochote kilichotokea, na nilihisi uzio wa uchoyo ukinuka moyoni mwangu.

Cynicism

Leo, uchoyo unamaanisha mwelekeo wa kuamini vibaya kuhusu watu na hali. Watu wachoyo wanaamini kwamba watu wote wamelengwa kabisa na ubinafsi na kwamba matukio mabaya yataendelea kuendelea.

Daktari wengi vijana wana matumaini na wana matumaini makubwa. Wanaamini kwamba wakifanya juhudi kubwa kabisa, wanaweza kufanya mabadiliko mazuri katika maisha ya wagonjwa wao. Kwa bahati mbaya, kadri muda unavyopita na wanajaribu kwa bidii na wagonjwa wao hawabadiliki, wanaweza kukata tamaa. Waganga hawa bado wanajaribu, lakini hawana tena matumaini kwamba juhudi zao zitatoa tofauti kubwa.

Mara nyingine uchoyo huu umeelekezwa dhidi ya wanasiasa wote. Wengine ni hasira tu dhidi ya wanachama wa chama kinachopingana na mienendo ya chama chao. Matumaini yanachukuliwa na uchoyo.

Cynicism in the Bible

Ikiwa kuna kitabu katika Biblia kinachoonekana kama kimeandikwa na mtu mwenye uchoyo, ni kitabu cha Mhubiri. Mhubiri, ambaye tunaelewa kuwa ni Sulemani, anaorodhesha mambo yote aliyoyajaribu kwa lengo la kupata furaha.

Katika sura ya 2:17-23 Sulemani anatafsiri kazi kama bure. Anamalizia akisema, “For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he hath laboured under the sun? For all his days are sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.” (Ecclesiastes 2:22,23)

Aliiona dunia ikiwa inatawaliwa na watawala na kulikuwa na kidogo ambacho watu wangeweza kufanya kuhusu hilo. Sulemani alianza hata kusema kwamba mamlaka ya kisiasa haikuwa na maana “Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished. For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also he that is born in his kingdom becometh poor” (Ecclesiastes 4:13).

Katika Mhubiri 6:6, anaonekana kumdharau maisha marefu. “Yea, though he live a thousand years twice told, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?”

Hakika, anamaliza kitabu chake kifupi kwa maagizo ya kumkumbuka Muumba wetu tunapokuwa vijana. Kuna baraka kwa wale wanaochagua kumtambua Mungu wakibaki na kidogo cha nguvu, badala ya sawa, wakati wanapokomaa na kuchoka, kama Sulemani.

Baadaye, ilionekana karibu kama Mungu alikuwa amekata tamaa kwa watu Wake. Hakuwaacha bila kutuma manabii, lakini alijua bila shaka kwamba watu wangekataa kujibu. “Therefore thou shalt speak all these words unto them; but they will not hearken to thee: thou shalt also call unto them; but they will not answer thee” (Jeremiah 7:27).

Hata katika Agano Jipya, Paulo alisema kwa Timotheo kwamba wakati uko ukaribu watu hawatatilia maanani mafundisho ya busara. “For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears;” (2 Timothy 4:3).

Kwa kuchagua na kupiga vichwa katikati ya vifungu hivi, tunaweza kutoka na mtazamo mzito wa giza wa siku zijazo na, zaidi hasa, kuhusu utayari wa binadamu kubadilika. Inaonekana hakuna faida kubwa ya kuwekeza tunaotaka katika watu waliotuzunguka. Wamejaa huzuni na wana uwezekano mdogo wa kubadilika kama chipmunk akifanikisha hesabu tofauti.

The Opposite of Cynicism

Kinyume cha uchoyo ni matumaini. Ni imani kwamba siku zijazo zinaweza kuwa bora.

Ni jambo la kuvutia kwamba Mtume Paulo alizungumza kuhusu dhiki katika Waraka kwa Waroma, “And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope: and hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us” (Romans 5:3-5).

Hatujafikia mahali ambapo tunakuwa tukifurahia katika majaribu tunayoyapitia, lakini bila shaka, yanapaswa kutuletea vitu vingine anavyozitaja. Kwa maana, tunakua kwa uvumilivu na uzoefu, hata tunapoendelea kukabiliana na majaribu, lakini zaidi ya hayo, tunatambua kwamba tuna matumaini ya kesho kwa sababu tunamtumikia Mungu mkuu.

Tofauti katika hadithi ya Mvulana Mwendawazimu katika Luka 15 inatufundisha mengi kuhusu matumaini. Baba na kaka mkubwa walikuwa tofauti kwa mhemko wao.

Baba hakuwahi kuacha matumaini—alijua kuwa mwanaye alikuwa amemkosea na kwenda mbali na kile alichojua kuwa sahihi na hata hivyo, baba bado alitamani kuona aliyepotea akirejea nafsi yake na kurudi nyumbani.

Kinyume chake, kaka mkubwa hakuwa na matumaini kwa kaka yake mdogo, na pia alikuwa na hasira kwake. Mwendawazimu alikuwa ametumia pesa zake, alikuwa ameishi kwa dhambi, na sasa, alirejea nyumbani kwa sababu tu hakuwa na pesa.

Hakika, hakukuwa na sababu ya kumwamini mwana mdogo. Lakini, hiyo ndicho hasa Bwana wetu wa Mbinguni anachofanya kwetu.

Look for Hope in the Right Places

Sehemu ya tatizo ni kwamba tunatafuta matumaini katika sehemu zisizofaa. Miaka kadhaa iliyopita, mgombea wa urais aliomba wadhifa kwa kauli mbiu “Hope and Change,” na ingawa alichaguliwa, nadhani watu wengi hawakuhisi maisha yao yalibadilika sana kwa heri.

Kukufuata mambo ambayo dunia inathamini—nguvu za kisiasa na utajiri kunahakikisha kuleta upweke. Huu ni mfano wa Shetani—daima anaahidi kupita kiasi na kutokamilisha ahadi.

Hili ndilo alilofanya alipomjaribu Yesu, “All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me” (Matthew 4:8). Mambo yote ambayo Shetani alitoa, hakuna kilicholinganishwa na utukufu ambao Yesu hatimaye alipokea kutoka kwa njia iliyosababisha msalaba.

Kwa njia ileile, Shetani angependa kumshawishi Mkristo asiyejitahidi kutafuta vitu vinavyothaminiwa, ambavyo vitaleta matumaini. Shetani anamwambia Mkristo kwamba siasa si tu zitabadilisha dunia kwa heri, bali ni njia rahisi ya kubadilisha dunia.

Biblia inaeleza wazi kwamba tunajenga matumaini tunapouza mahusiano yetu na Mungu kisha tukafanya kazi kumsaidia ndugu na dada zetu kujenga uhusiano huo katika maisha yao. Sababu tunayo matumaini sio kwa sababu watu ni wazuri sana—hatuhitaji kuishi muda mrefu kuelewa kuwa hawako. Sababu tuna matumaini ni kwa sababu tunamtumikia Mungu mwenye kushangaza, mwaminifu ambaye anatembea pamoja nasi kupitia majaribu mabaya kabisa.

Remember that We Have Undeserved Hope

Ujumbe wa Yesu kuhusu msamaha unaweka wazi kwamba moja ya sababu kuu tunazotakiwa kusamehe wengine ni kwamba tumepokea msamaha mkubwa usio na sifa. Hilo pia ni kweli kwa matumaini.

Kila mmoja wetu alikuwa hana matumaini na hakukuwa na sababu ya kutegemea kupata matumaini na bado tulipewa mwanga mdogo katikati ya giza letu. Labda sehemu ya sababu tunapata ugumu wa kuwa na matumaini kwa ajili ya watu waliotuzunguka ni kwamba hatukumbuki jinsi tulivyokuwa bila matumaini kabla hatujapata neema.

Ikiwa Yesu aliweza kuleta matumaini kwenye maisha yetu yasiyo na matumaini, basi bila shaka Yeye anaweza kufanya mambo makubwa katika mioyo na maisha ya wengine waliotuzunguka. Watu pekee tunawalazimika kuacha ni wale ambao Mwokozi wetu pia amewaacha.

Small Efforts Do Make a Difference

Nakumbuka nilikuwa na mazungumzo na kijana aliyekuwa anapanga kuingia katika tiba na alikuwa na mpango wa kwenda nchi ya kigeni kumuhudumia watu huko. Tulipokuwa tukizungumza, mtu mzee aliingia kwenye mazungumzo na akasema kuwa hakuona matumaini mengi ya mabadiliko katika nchi zinazoendelea.

Watu katika nchi hizi walikuwa hawana hamu ya kujiboresha na hawafanyi kile cha chini kinachohitajika kuzuia mambo kama kuambukizwa na minyoo na vimelea. Madaktari na wauguzi hawawezi kuleta tofauti katika mazingira kama hayo.

Niliweza kuhisi moyo wa kijana huyo ukishuka alipomshirikisha huyu mzee. Alikuwa na uzoefu, na alikuwa amekata tamaa. Kinachosikitisha ni kwamba alikuwa pia anampora matumaini mtu aliyekuwa bado na tamaa ya kuhudumia.

Nilikulia nikiwa niko kwenye mafunzo, nilikuwa na upasuaji alinieleza kwamba madaktari wa familia hawafanya chochote kweli. Walikuwa tu wakiwarudia wagonjwa wao hadi ziara yao inayofuata, wakati upasuaji kweli uliwafanyia watu “kurekebisha”—kuondoa kiungo kilichosababisha tatizo.

Mwisho wa siku, juhudi ndogo za kufanya kazi zinatenda tofauti. Sifanyi upasuaji wa ubongo, lakini bado ninaweza kuleta tofauti katika maisha ya mtu mwingine—labda kwa kutumia muda kidogo kusikiliza na kuomba. Hii ni kweli kwa sisi sote.

Zaidi ya hayo, tunatambua kwamba kufanya juhudi hizi kunabadilisha maisha yetu wenyewe kwa heri. Yesu alisema kwa kondoo kwamba wanapomtunzia “wadogo miongoni mwa ndugu zangu”, walikuwa wamtumikia Yeye.

Hata kama maisha ya mtu hayana mabadiliko, Mwokozi wetu anajua tamaa zetu na anahisi juhudi zetu, na atazitegemea siku moja.

A Few Things to Remember

Tunapokabili kushindwa, huenda tukajikuta tunasonga katika mwelekeo mmoja wa kati. Watu wetu wana optimisti wanaonekana kuamini kuwa tukio hili lilikuwa tukio la pekee na kwamba siku zijazo bado ni angavu. Kwa upande mwingine, wavimbi wanaamini kwamba kushindwa ni kudumu, binafsi, na kunatambaa.

Wavimbi wanaamini kwamba kushindwa kwao ni matokeo ya dosari za tabia zao walizozaliwa nazo na kwamba mambo hayaathiri maisha yao yote na hayatafanywa kubadilika. Tofauti na mtu mwenye haki ambaye anashuka ili kuinuka tena, watu hawa wanashuka na kukaa pale waliposhuka, wamepoteza mapema kabla ya kuanza.

Tunapokuwa tukishughulika na watu wengine, tunahitaji kuwapa neema ile ile tunayopaswa kupewa sisi wenyewe. Wao pia wanakua, na ikiwa wana kushindwa leo, watafanya vizuri kesho. Labda watafeli tena, lakini angalau watashindwa “kwa njia bora.”

Conclusion

Uchoyo umeenea katika dunia yetu. Wengi wameshindwa kuendelea na matumaini kwa siku zijazo bora, na inaweza kueleweka kwa wale walioweka matumaini yao katika taasisi za dunia. Hakuna tumaini halisi katika serikali au katika majeshi au katika utumishi wa umma.

Wimbo unasema, “Oh to have no hope in Jesus, how dark this world must be!” Kwa maana, Yesu ndiye anayeleta mwanga kwenye giza letu na kuturuhusu kuendelea, hata wakati wengine wanatutia hasara.

Mungu ndiye anayetuokoa. Yeye ndiye aliemtuma manabii, ingawa ujumbe wao ulikataliwa, na manabii waladhulumiwa. Yeye ndiye anayebaki kuwa na matumaini yetu, hata tukiwa tumewakosesha mara nyingi katika zamani.

Yeye ndiye sababu tunafuata mbele. Yeye ndiye sababu tuna matumaini, si tu kwa ajili yetu bali pia kwa ndugu zetu.

How unbelievable it is that God can take a wretched sinner, void of the fear of the Lord, and turn him into a blood-washed saint and preacher of the gospel! In this story, we see God’s life-changing power at work in our hymn writer’s life.

In the small cemetery of a churchyard in Olney, England, stands a granite tombstone with this inscription, written by Newton himself before his death:

John Newton, once an infidel and libertine, a servant of slaves in Africa, was, by the rich mercy of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, preserved, restored, pardoned, and appointed to preach the faith he had long labored to destroy!

This epitaph aptly describes the unusual and colorful life of this man, one of the great evangelical preachers of the eighteenth century. His testimony was, “By the grace of God, I am what I am!”

“Amazing Grace” was a hymn published in 1779, with words written in 1772 by the English poet and Anglican clergyman John Newton (1725–1807). “Amazing Grace” is probably the most beloved hymn of the last two centuries. This hymn is estimated to be performed 10 million times annually. It has appeared on over 11,000 albums and translated into about 60 languages. It was referenced in Harriet Beecher Stowe’s anti-slavery novel Uncle Tom’s Cabin. It had a surge in popularity during two of America’s greatest crises: the Civil War and the Vietnam War.

Ironically, this stirring song, closely associated with the African-American community, was written by a former slave trader, John Newton.

John was born on July 24, 1725, in Wapping, England, to a seafaring father, John Newton, Sr., and a devout Christian mother, Elizabeth Newton. His father loved him but was gone at sea most of the time. On the other hand, his mother was tender and nurturing, teaching him the Word of God. She would instruct him in memorizing the Bible whole chapters at a time and took him to church. Unfortunately, when he was almost seven, his mother died of tuberculosis. His father remarried a short time later and sent him to a boarding school. During his time at the boarding school, he made bad friends. His character disintegrated to the point that he was dismissed from one school and moved to another. By the time he was 11 years old, the boarding schools didn’t want him, so his father took him along to sea. He spent the next six years on the Atlantic Ocean with his father.

When John was 17, his father arranged to send him to Jamaica for a well-paying job overseeing a plantation. On his way, while waiting for the ship’s departure, John received an invitation to the home of some old-time friends, the Catletts. It was in this home that John’s mother had died ten years earlier. As he reacquainted himself with them, he got to know their daughter, Mary. John and Mary’s mothers were best of friends. John had been invited to stay four days, but he stayed two weeks and missed the ship to Jamaica.

At age 18, John was conscripted into the Royal Navy, and his life went from bad to worse. He wanted to return and see Mary, so he deserted the ship but was caught, publicly flogged, and laid in irons. His life on the ship was so profane that even the other ungodly sailors cringed at his curses and blasphemies. He gained the title “The Great Blasphemer” and was such an unwanted man on the ship that he was sent to work on a slave ship.

One of the owners of the slave ship where he now worked, offered John a job once they reached the African coast. However, once on shore, he was tied up and forced to work with little food, clothing, or shelter. He sent several letters back to his father during this time, pleading for help.

A ship called The Greyhound was sailing near the coast, which John had now called home. The captain had been instructed by John’s father to look for his son. The ship, while being almost too far from shore to trade, decided to give trading a try. A friend of John’s rowed out from shore to trade. As he turned to leave, the captain asked him whether he knew anyone named John Newton. He did to the captain’s surprise, and John was brought on board to go home.

On board the ship, Newton picked up a copy of Thomas á Kempis’s Christian classic, The Imitation of Christ. He had never encountered anything like it, and he began to wonder if the Christian claims might be true. That night, on March 10, 1748, a fierce storm nearly swamped the ship. Men, animals, and provisions were swept overboard. The storm awakened Newton, the ship’s rotten timbers broken by the waves and floodwater swirling into his cabin. John prayed for the first time in years.

The Greyhound thrashed about in the North Atlantic storm for over 11 days. With little hope of survival, the sailors mechanically worked the pumps, trying to keep the vessel afloat. On the eleventh day of the storm, John was too exhausted to pump, so he was tied to the helm, where he did his best to hold the ship to its course. From one o’clock until midnight, he was at the helm. He feared he was going to die, and if the Christian faith were true, then he surely would not be forgiven. He reflected on all he had done over the past few years. His life seemed as ruined and wrecked as the battered ship he was trying to steer through the storm. During those long and grueling hours, Newton cried out to God like he never had before, and that was the turning point in his life.

That was a day John Newton remembered ever after. “On that day, the Lord sent from on high and delivered me out of deep waters.” Over 50 years later, John wrote in his diary on March 21, 1805: “Not well able to write; but I endeavor to observe the return of this day with humiliation, prayer, and praise.”

Only God’s amazing grace could take a rude, profane, slave-trading sailor and transform him into a child of God. John never ceased to stand in awe of God’s work in his life. He took an interest in prayer, reading and meditating on the Scriptures, and only speaking words pleasing to God.

On his return home, Mary and her parents recognized the change the Lord had brought in John. The two were married on February 1, 1750.

For the next four years, Newton was captain of his own slave ship. This occupation kept him separated from Mary for months at a time. While they were apart, the two corresponded constantly. In his letters, John repeatedly wrote how their love and marriage increased his thankfulness and gratefulness to the Lord. “... When I indulge myself with a particular thought of you, it usually carries me on farther and brings me upon my knees to bless the Lord for giving me such a treasure and to pray for your peace and welfare”

John endeavored to “Christianize” his slave ship by holding Sunday services for his crew of 30 sin-hardened men. He made three more voyages to bring slaves from Africa to North America. As he planned his fourth trip, he became sick with malaria. God used this sickness to end his involvement in the slave trade.

As John began a new chapter in his life, he felt called to be a minister. For more than 50 years, he preached the gospel and was one of the most influential men of his day.

John Newton often composed a hymn to go with his Sunday evening services. In 1779, 280 of these were collected and combined with 68 hymns by Newton’s friend and parishioner, William Cowper, and published as the Olney Hymns. The most famous of all the Olney Hymns, “Faith’s Review and Expectation”, grew out of David’s exclamation in 1 Chronicles 17:16-17. We know it today as “Amazing Grace”. “Amazing Grace” originally had six stanzas, and the last verse was added about a century later. Most hymnals have four or five of these verses.

As minister in the church, John continued to be more and more troubled by the slave trade that was still going on. In 1788, 34 years after he left the slave trade, He wrote a book entitled Thoughts Upon the African Slave Trade and sent it to all the members of parliament. This book brought an awareness to the public of the evils of the slave trade. He quotes this, “Needless to say, the capturing, selling and transporting of black slaves to the plantations in the West Indies and America was a cruel and vicious way of life.” With the help and providence of God, John saw the day, several months before his death, in 1807, when slavery was officially banned from England.

When John was in his sixties, his beloved wife Mary passed away. This was a great trial for John, and he spent the remaining 17 years of his life without her.

After John suffered a stroke and shortly before his death, a spokesman for the church encouraged Newton to consider retiring from preaching because of failing health, eyesight, and memory. John replied, “What, shall the old African blasphemer stop while he can still speak? I will continue to preach. Although my memory’s fading, I remember two things very clearly: I am a great sinner, and Christ is a great Savior.”

The last words of John Newton as he lay on his deathbed were as follows: “I am still in the land of the dying; I shall be in the land of the living soon.”

The tune “Amazing Grace” is an early American folk melody. It was first known as a plantation melody entitled “Loving Lambs”. This tune was first published in 1831 in the book The Virginia Harmony. The majority of hymn books published after this time included this song. In 1910, Edwin O. Excell added the last verse, which eventually replaced the last three original verses of the song. His edition of the song is most common in our hymnals today. Several other Olney hymns by Newton continue to be sung today, including “How Sweet the Name of Jesus Sounds” and “Glorious Things of Thee are Spoken”.

Ni ajabu kiasi gani kwamba Mungu anaweza kumchukua mwenye dhambi mwovu, asiye na hofu ya Bwana, na kumfanya kuwa mtakatifu aliyefutwa kwa damu na mhubiri wa injili! Katika hadithi hii tunaona nguvu ya Mungu inayobadilisha maisha ikifanya kazi katika maisha ya mwandishi wetu wa nyimbo.

Kwenye makaburi madogo ya uwanja wa kanisa huko Olney, Uingereza, kuna jiwe la kaburi la graniti lenye maandishi haya, yaliyoandikwa na Newton mwenyewe kabla ya kifo chake:

John Newton, aliwahi kuwa mkosefu wa imani na mtenda maovu, mtumishi wa watumwa Afrika, alihifadhiwa, akarejeshwa, akasamehewa, na kuwekwa kuhubiri imani aliyekuwa akijaribu kuharibu kwa huruma nyingi za Bwana na Mwokozi wetu Yesu Kristo!

Maandishi haya ya kaburi yanaelezea kwa ufanisi maisha yasiyo ya kawaida na yenye rangi za mwanaume huyu, mmoja wa wahubiri wakuu wa kimisionari wa karne ya kumi na nane. Ushuhuda wake ulikuwa, “Kwa neema ya Mungu, mimi ni kile ninachokuwa!”

“Amazing Grace” ilikuwa wimbo uliyochapishwa mwaka 1779, na maneno yaliyoandikwa mwaka 1772 na mshairi wa Kiingereza na mchungaji wa Anglican John Newton (1725–1807). “Amazing Grace” pengine ni wimbo ulioipendwa zaidi katika karne mbili zilizopita. Wimbo huu unakadiriwa kuimbwa mara milioni 10 kila mwaka. Umeonekana kwenye albamu zaidi ya 11,000 na kutafsiriwa katika takriban lugha 60. Ulitajwa katika riwaya ya kupinga utumwa ya Harriet Beecher Stowe, Uncle Tom’s Cabin. Ulishuhudia kushuka kwa umaarufu wake katika wakati wa misukosuko mibaya miwili ya Marekani: Vita vya Mwaka wa 1861–1865 (Civil War) na Vita vya Vietnam.

Kinyume chake, wimbo huu wenye msisimko, unaohusishwa kwa karibu na jamii ya Wamarekani-Marekani ya asili ya Afrika, uliandikwa na mfanyabiashara wa watumwa wa zamani, John Newton.

John alizaliwa Julai 24, 1725, huko Wapping, Uingereza, kwa baba mwepesi wa kama meli, John Newton, Sr., na mama mwaminifu wa Kikristo, Elizabeth Newton. Baba yake alimpenda lakini alikuwa baharini kwa sehemu kubwa ya wakati. Kwa upande mwingine, mamake alikuwa mpole na mwenye huruma, akimfundisha Neno la Mungu. Alimfundisha kukumbuka Biblia kwa sura nzima kwa wakati mmoja na kumpeleka kanisani. Kwa bahati mbaya, alipokuwa karibu na umri wa miaka saba, mamake alifariki kwa kifua kikuu. Baba yake alifunga ndoa tena muda mfupi baadaye na akamtuma shule ya malezi. Wakati wa kusoma yake, alikutana na marafiki wabaya. Tabia yake ilivunjika hadi kiwango kwamba alitupwa kutoka shule moja na kuhamishwa nyingine. Alipofikia miaka 11, shule za malezi hazikumtaka tena, hivyo baba yake akamchukua baharini. Alitumia miaka sita iliyofuata kwenye Bahari ya Atlantiki akiwa na baba yake.

Alipokuwa na miaka 17, baba yake alipanga kumtuma Jamaica kwa kazi yenye malipo mazuri ya kusimamia shamba. Njiani, akiwa akisubiri kuondoka kwa meli, John alipokea mwaliko wa kukaa nyumbani kwa marafiki wa zamani, familia Catlett. Ilikuwa katika nyumba hii ambapo mamake alikuwa amefariki miaka kumi kabla. Alipojipatanisha nao tena, aliyafahamu binti yao, Mary. Mama wa John na mama wa Mary walikuwa marafiki wakubwa. John alikuwa amualikwa kukaa siku nne, lakini alikaa wiki mbili na akakosa meli ya kuelekea Jamaica.

Alipofikisha umri wa miaka 18, John alichaguliwa kwa lazima kujiunga na Jeshi la Majini la Ufalme (Royal Navy), na maisha yake yalibadilika kwa mbaya zaidi. Alitaka kurudi na kumuona Mary, hivyo alitoroka meli lakini alikamatwa, akachapwa hadharani kwa fimbo, na kuwekwa kwa mketi. Maisha yake kwenye meli yalikuwa ya uzinifu kiasi kwamba hata wapiganaji wenzake wasio wa Mungu walitisha kwa laana zake na kuchukia matamshi yake ya kuasi. Alipata cheo cha “Mkasiri Mkuu wa Uasi” na alikuwa mtu asiyehitajika kwenye meli kiasi kwamba alitumwa kufanya kazi kwenye meli ya watumwa.

Mmoja wa wamiliki wa meli ya watumwa ambapo sasa alikuwa akifanya kazi, alimpa John kazi mara walipofika pwani ya Afrika. Hata hivyo, alinifikwa na kamba alipofika kisiwa na kulazimishwa kufanya kazi akiwa amefungwa, akiwa na chakula kidogo, nguo chache, na makazi duni. Alituma barua kadhaa kwa baba yake wakati huo, akimwomba msaada.

Meli moja iitwayo The Greyhound ilikuwa ikisafiri karibu na pwani, ambayo John sasa alikuwa ameita nyumbani. Kapteni alikuwa amepokea maagizo na baba yake ya kutafuta mwanawe. Meli, ingawa ilikuwa karibu sana na pwani kwa ajili ya biashara, iliamua kujaribu kufanya biashara. Rafiki wa John alikuja kwa mashua kutoka pwani kuingia kufanya biashara. Alipogeuka kuondoka, kapteni akamwuliza kama anajua mtu aitwaye John Newton. Rafiki yake alijua kwa mshangao wa kapteni, na John alileta meli ili arudi nyumbani.

Ndani ya meli, Newton alipata nakala ya kitabu cha kikristo cha Thomas á Kempis, The Imitation of Christ. Hakuwahi kukutana na kitu kama hicho, na alianza kutafakari kama dai la Kikristo linaweza kuwa kweli. Usiku huo, Machi 10, 1748, dhoruba kali karibu ilitimua meli. Wanaume, wanyama, na vitu vya chakula vilitetemwa baharini. Dhoruba ilimfufua Newton, mbao mbovu za meli zikavunjika na maji ya mafuriko yakazunguka ndani ya kabati yake. John aliaomba kwa mara ya kwanza kwa miaka mingi.

The Greyhound ilitetemeka katika dhoruba ya Bahari Kaskazini kwa zaidi ya siku 11. Kwa matumaini kidogo ya kuishi, walinzi wa meli walifanya kazi za pampu kwa mitambo, wakijaribu kuifanya meli kuwa juu ya maji. Siku ya kumi na moja ya dhoruba, John alikuwa amelegea kupanda, hivyo akafungwa kwenye kiwambo, ambapo alijitahidi kadri ya uwezo wake kushikilia meli kwenye mwelekeo wake. Kuanzia saa moja hadi usiku wa manane, alikuwa kwenye kiwambo. Alikuwa na hofu ya kufa, na kama imani ya Kikristo ingeweza kuwa ya kweli, basi hakika hangepatwa na msamaha. Alikumbuka yote aliyoyafanya katika miaka ya hivi karibuni. Maisha yake yalionekana kuwa yamaharibika na kuvunjika kama meli iliyokandamizwa aliyekuwa akijaribu kuiendesha kupitia dhoruba. Katika masaa yale marefu na magumu, Newton aliomba kwa Mungu kwa njia ambayo hakuwahi kufanya hapo awali, na huo ulikuwa mwambao wa maisha yake.

Huo ulikuwa siku ambayo John Newton alikumbuka milele. “Siku hiyo, Bwana alituma kutoka juu na akanitoa katika maji ya kina.” Zaidi ya miaka 50 baadaye, John aliandika katika jarida lake tarehe Machi 21, 1805: “Siwezi kuandika vizuri; lakini najitahidi kukumbuka kurudi kwa siku hii kwa unyenyekevu, maombi, na sifa.”

Ni neema ya Mungu tu iliyoweza kumchukua mlezi mwenye adabu mbaya, mwenye uzinifu, mfanyabiashara wa watumwa na kumgeuza kuwa mtoto wa Mungu. John hakuwahi kuacha kushangazwa na kazi ya Mungu katika maisha yake. Alianzisha hamu ya maombi, kusoma na kutafakari Maandiko, na kuongea maneno tu yanayompendeza Mungu.

Akiwa amerudi nyumbani, Mary na wazazi wake walitambua mabadiliko aliyoyaleta Bwana kwa John. Wawili hao waliolewa Februari 1, 1750.

Kwa miaka minne iliyofuata, Newton alikuwa nahodha wa meli yake mwenyewe ya watumwa. Kazi hii ilimtoa mbali na Mary kwa miezi kadhaa mfululizo. Walipokuwa mbali, wawili hao waliendelea kuandika barua mara kwa mara. Katika barua zake, John aliandika mara kwa mara jinsi upendo wao na ndoa yao ulivyoongeza shukrani na moyo wa shukrani kwake kwa Bwana. “... Ninapomruhusu nafsi yangu kufikiria kwa undani yako, kwa kawaida hunileta mbali zaidi na kunileta kwa magoti kumshukuru Bwana kwa kunipatia hazina kama hiyo na kumuomba Bwana ampe amani yako na ustawi wako”

John alijaribu “kukristoisha” meli yake ya watumwa kwa kuandaa ibada za Jumapili kwa ajili ya wafanyakazi wake 30 waliokuwa wamejikunja kwa dhambi. Alifanya safari tatu zaidi kuleta watumwa kutoka Afrika kwenda Amerika Kaskazini. Alipokuwa akipanga safari yake ya nne, akapatwa na malaria. Mungu alitumia ugonjwa huu kumaliza ushiriki wake katika biashara ya watumwa.

Akiingia katika sura mpya ya maisha yake, alihisi anaitwa kuwa mchungaji. Kwa zaidi ya miaka 50, alihubiri injili na alikuwa mmoja wa watu wenye ushawishi mkubwa wa wakati wake.

John Newton mara nyingi aliandika wimbo kuendana na ibada zake za Jumapili jioni. Mwaka 1779, nyimbo 280 kati ya hizi zilikusanywa na kuunganishwa na nyimbo 68 za rafiki na mwanachama wa parokia ya Newton, William Cowper, na kuchapishwa kama Olney Hymns. Iliyo maarufu zaidi kati ya Olney Hymns, “Faith’s Review and Expectation”, ilitokana na exclamation ya Daudi katika 1 Mambo ya Nyakati 17:16-17. Tunaiifahamu leo kama “Amazing Grace”. “Amazing Grace” awali ilikuwa na mistari sita, na beti ya mwisho iliongezwa takriban karne moja baadaye. Vitabu vya nyimbo vingi vina beti nne au tano za nyimbo hizi.

Kama mchungaji wa kanisa, John aliendelea kuzidi kuumizwa na biashara ya watumwa ambayo bado ilikuwa ikiendelea. Mwaka 1788, miaka 34 baada ya kuacha biashara ya watumwa, aliandika kitabu kilichoitwa Thoughts Upon the African Slave Trade na kukituma kwa wajumbe wote wa bunge. Kitabu hiki kilileta uelewa kwa umma juu ya mabaya ya biashara ya watumwa. Ananukuu hii, “Bila shaka, kukamata, kuuza na kusafirisha watumwa weusi kwenda mashambani katika Visiwa vya Magharibi na Amerika ilikuwa njia ya maisha yenye ukatili na ujeuri.” Kwa msaada na muongozo wa Mungu, John aliona siku, miezi kadhaa kabla ya kifo chake, mwaka 1807, wakati utumwa ulipofutwa rasmi nchini Uingereza.

John alipokuwa katika miaka ya sitini, mke wake mpendwa Mary alifariki. Hii ilikuwa jaribu kubwa kwa John, na alitumia miaka 17 iliyobaki ya maisha yake bila yeye.

Baada ya John kupata kiharusi na na kabla ya kifo chake, msemaji wa kanisa alimshurutisha Newton afikirie kustaafu kuhubiri kwa sababu ya afya inayoshuka, kuona kuchosha, na kumbukumbu. John alijibu, “Nini, je, mkasiri wa zamani wa Afrika ataacha wakati bado anaweza kuzungumza? Nitaendelea kuhubiri. Ingawa kumbukumbu yangu inaanza kutoweka, nakumbuka vitu viwili kwa uwazi: mimi ni mtenda dhambi mkubwa, na Kristo ni Mwokoa mkuu.”

Maneno ya mwisho ya John Newton alipolala kitandani kwa kifo yalikuwa kama haya: “Bado nipo katika nchi ya wanaokufa; hivi karibuni nitakuwa katika nchi ya wanaoishi.”

Melodi ya “Amazing Grace” ni ala ya mapema ya muziki wa asili ya Amerika. Ilijulikana kwanza kama melodi ya shamba ikiitwa “Loving Lambs”. Melodi hii ilichapishwa kwa mara ya kwanza mwaka 1831 katika kitabu The Virginia Harmony. Wingi wa vitabu vya nyimbo vilivyochapishwa baada ya wakati huu vilijumuisha wimbo huu. Mwaka 1910, Edwin O. Excell aliongeza beti ya mwisho, ambayo hatimaye ilibadilisha beti tatu za asili za mwisho za wimbo. Toleo lake la wimbo ndio linalopatikana zaidi katika vitabu vyetu vya nyimbo leo. Nyimbo nyingine kadhaa za Olney za Newton zinaendelea kuimbwa hadi leo, ikiwemo “How Sweet the Name of Jesus Sounds” na “Glorious Things of Thee are Spoken”.

Do you believe in miracles? Do you believe in the supernatural? What about divine intervention? Or a better question might be, have you seen God working in your life? Do others see God working in your life?

My brother was working in the greenhouse when a customer walked in and marveled at the beauty of all the plants. He then exclaimed how impressed he was at all our hard work. My brother responded with, “Some plant, some water, but God gives the increase.” To which the customer responded with, “No, no, don’t give the credit to God. You came out here and did all this work. You planted, watered, and fertilized all these plants, and you all deserve the credit, not God!” The reason the man felt this way is because he was a humanist.

What is Humanism?

The dictionary defines humanism like this; an outlook or system of thought attaching prime importance to human rather than divine or supernatural matters. Humanist beliefs stress the potential value and goodness of human beings, emphasize common human needs, and seek solely rational ways of solving human problems.

If God does exist, then we will have to recognize this fact and answer to Him. Humanists attempt to prove that God does not exist, so they can freely live their lives as they please. According to humanism, there is no God. If so, then we, the human race, are superior to God. Everything is for us and our ultimate happiness. This is the definition of humanism.

Two Types of Humanism

There are two types of humanistic beliefs, and we will look at both. The first belief is the theory that there is no God. In reality, this seems to be the only rational way to be a humanist. Everything is created by man and for man. There are no other factors or supernatural involvement. Everything happens by reason and common sense. There is a logical explanation for everything that happens. Of course, some things do not make sense, but humanists brush those aside and look only at the things that can be explained. Like the plants in the greenhouse, they look at all that man does and ignore the supernatural part of a plant springing forth with new life. Scientists around the world are working diligently to put human reasoning into everything that has ever happened, even the creation of the world. Scientists, with all their learning and wisdom, attempt to give logical explanations for why natural disasters and global crises happen. If they can explain everything, then they can rule out God and His existence. This allows the human race to do as it pleases without eternal consequences. This, in turn leads to a great sense of false peace.

The humanists, with all their reasoning, mock the very existence of God. If you go to most colleges in America and talk to people about Christianity, they laugh at you and mock the fact that Christians actually believe in God.

The second type of humanistic belief is a theory of humanism that acknowledges the existence of God. One anthropologist argued that humanism is a project of modernity and a secularized continuation of Western Christian theology. But if you ask people what they think humanism means, you will likely get different responses, and it becomes very confusing. But why the confusion? Because people are trying to be Christian humanists. Christian Humanism has frequently been criticized for its vagueness and difficulty to define. The reason it has become so confusing is that people want to believe in God but also believe in themselves and that the world revolves around them.

In Romans, we read, “For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet. And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient; Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them” (Romans 1:18-32).

So how can one be a humanist and believe in God? This is where we hit a little closer to home. This type of humanist believes God wants him to be happy. He believes in a Creator God but does not believe he has to serve Him In reality. He doesn’t believe in the true God but, in his mind, created a fictitious god that does not exist. This allows him to live for himself and his own happiness. This type of person will talk about God, go to church, sing songs, and say prayers. However, he will look only to man for all his needs. If he is sick, he calls a doctor. If he needs money, he goes to the banker. If the need is a break from reality, he takes a vacation or retreat. He lives life for his own happiness and then thanks God though he did not look to God for his needs. These people are dependent on themselves. They have confidence in themselves.

Here is an example: A Christian plants a garden and takes care of it each day. He waters and fertilizes weeds and prunes. Finally, his plants all begin to bear fruit, nice fruit. He thanks God for the plentiful harvest. His neighbor, an atheistic humanist, also planted a garden. He, too, went out each day and watered, pruned, weeded, and fertilized. He also received a bountiful harvest. This man, however, boasted of all that he had accomplished. Both men did the same things and had similar results. One gave God the credit, and one credited himself. He will say he accomplished the same thing without God that his neighbor did with God. Christians know that he is wrong and that he actually did need God to grow his garden.

When something happens that requires supernatural intervention, the Christian humanist prays and asks others to pray. However, he does not believe God will answer their prayers and instantly gets to work to solve his problem, with only human reasoning. Then, if the problem is resolved, he thanks God for it. This type of humanism has confused the modern world. It has caused unbelievers to mock the Christian faith and to call it a false religion with no power.

The Christian does not believe in human reasoning. The Christian believes that the God of heaven is the reason for everything. “For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him” (Colossians 1:16). We are nothing without Him, and without Him, we can do nothing. Christianity is the opposite of humanism. When the Christian does something supernatural, something the humanist or atheist cannot do, then we have something that will confound the wise.

When the neighbor sees the Christian loving his enemies, forgiving someone who wronged him, and doing things that he cannot do, he then begins to wonder where the power to do these things came from. This then leads him to the Father. When there is nothing supernatural that we are doing, he is confused.

What About Us?

I fear that we are falling into this trap of ‘Christian Humanism.’ We talk the talk; we say we believe in God. We go to church, sing songs, and say prayers. However, from outward appearances, we trust in ourselves. Because we have centered our lives around ourselves and our well-being, the God of heaven does not hear us. Our prayers are not answered, and the time on our knees is a struggle at best. We go through the motions because that is how we’ve been taught, but our faith lies in human reasoning.

It can be extremely difficult to seek the Lord while living in a humanistic society. A society that has perfected the pursuit of liberty and happiness. Slowly, the church is caving to the ways of this world.

A minister from China was visiting the churches in America. Before departing back to China, he was asked what impressed him most about the churches in America. He replied, “I am amazed at what all they have accomplished without God.”

We would do well to simplify the modern definition of humanism. The humanist proudly denies that there is a God when he boasts of his own strength and abilities. He proclaims the great accomplishments of man and mocks the humble Christian.

The Christian denies himself, picks up his cross, and follows his Master. The Christian thinks nothing of himself or the ability of man, confidently admitting that he is merely dust and back to that dust he will quickly go. The Christian looks for the good in others and trusts God for all his daily needs and cares.

Christians believe they are merely servants to their master. They are hated by the world and despised by most, rejected. “If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you. (John 15:18)” To them, this life is not the pursuit of happiness. The things of this world do not even interest them. Their joy and peace comes solely from serving their master, from pleasing their Heavenly Father. To the world, they are strange. Fools. To God, they are His dear children.

God is still looking for people today who will put their trust in Him. He is looking over all the earth for someone, somewhere, who will put aside human reasoning and common sense and obey the voice from heaven. God wants men with faith who will step out into the supernatural, like Abraham, Moses, David, and the thousands of believers that followed. Someone who will deny himself and this world and follow the Savior.

When this life is over, the humanists, whether they say they believe in God or not, will perish. And the Christians will go on to live forever in glory.

Humanist? Christian? Christian Humanist? Which one are you?

Je, unaamini maajabu? Je, unaamini katika kile kisicho cha kawaida? Je, kuhusu uingiliaji wa kimungu? Au swali bora linaweza kuwa, umewahi kuona Mungu akifanya kazi katika maisha yako? Je, wengine wanaona Mungu akifanya kazi katika maisha yako?

Mdogo wangu alikuwa akifanya kazi kwa kikombe cha mimea alipokuwa mteja akitoka na kushangazwa na uzuri wa mimea yote. Kisha alitamka jinsi alivyoshangazwa na kazi yetu yote. Mdogo wangu alijibu, “Mimi nimepanda, nimekucha, lakini Mungu hutoa ukuaji.” Mteja akajibu, “Hapana, hapana, usimguse Mungu kwa heshima hiyo. Ninyi mlikuja hapa mkafanya kazi hii yote. Niliyeitafuta, mlikucha, na mlilizunua maua haya yote, ninyi ndiyo mnafaiwa na sifa, si Mungu!” Sababu hii ndiyo maana mtu huyo alihisi hivyo kwa sababu alikuwa mwanahumanisti.

Humanismi ni Nini?

Kamusi inafafanua humanismu hivi; mtazamo au mfumo wa fikra unaoweka umuhimu mkuu kwa mambo ya kibinadamu badala ya ya kimungu au ya siri za ulimwengu. Imani za wanahumanisti zinaweka msisitizo kwa thamani na wema wa kibinadamu, zinaangazia mahitaji ya kawaida ya binadamu, na kutafuta njia za kimantiki pekee za kutatua matatizo ya binadamu.

Iwapo Mungu yupo, basi tutalazimika kutambua ukweli huu na kumjibu Yeye. Wanahumanisti wanajaribu kuthibitisha kwamba Mungu hayupo, ili waweze kuishi kwa uhuru kama wanavyotaka. Kulingana na humanismu, hakuna Mungu. Ikiwa ni hivyo, basi sisi, jinsia ya binadamu, tuko juu ya Mungu. Kila kitu ni kwa ajili yetu na furaha yetu ya mwisho. Hii ndiyo tafsiri ya humanismu.

Aina Mbili za Humanismu

Kuna aina mbili za imani za humanisti, na tutaangalia zote mbili. Imani ya kwanza ni nadharia kwamba hakuna Mungu. Kwa kweli, hii inaonekana kuwa njia pekee ya kimantiki ya kuwa mwanahumanisti. Kila kitu kimeundwa na mwanadamu na kwa mwanadamu. Hakuna sababu nyingine wala uingiliaji wa kimazingira. Kila kitu hutokea kwa mantiki na uchekeshaji wa kawaida. Kuna ufafanuzi wa kimantiki kwa kila kitu kinachotokea. Bila shaka, baadhi ya mambo hayafai kueleweka, lakini wanahumanisti huwa yanapuuza yale na kuangalia tu mambo yanayoweza kuelezewa. Kama mimea katika kikombe cha mimea, wanaangalia yale yote ambayo mwanadamu hufanya na kusahau sehemu ya kimungu ya mmea kuibuka na uhai mpya. Wanasayansi duniani kote wanafanya kazi kwa bidii kuweka mantiki ya binadamu katika kila kitu kilichowahi kutokea, hata uumbaji wa dunia. Wanasayansi, kwa elimu yao yote na busara, wanajaribu kutoa maelezo ya kimantiki kwa nini majanga ya asili na migogoro ya dunia hutokea. Ikiwa wanaweza kuelezea kila kitu, basi wanaweza kuondoa uwezekano wa Mungu na kuwepo kwake. Hii inawawezesha watu wa binadamu kufanya wanavyotaka bila matokeo ya milele. Hii, kwa upande mwingine, inasababisha hisia kubwa ya amani ya uongo.

Wanahumanisti, kwa mantiki yao yote, wanatafuna uwepo wa Mungu wenyewe. Ukifika katika chuo kikuu mengi nchini Amerika na ukaongea na watu kuhusu Ukristo, wanakutabasamu na kutesa ukweli kwamba Wakristo kwa kweli wanaamini katika Mungu.

Aina ya pili ya imani ya humanisti ni nadharia ya humanismu inayotambua uwepo wa Mungu. Mtu mmoja wa wanthropolojia alidai kwamba humanismu ni mradi wa kisasa na kuendelea kwa ule ukristo wa Magharibi uliofanyishwa sekulari. Lakini ukimuuliza watu wapi wanadhani humanismu inamaanisha, uwezekano utapata majibu tofauti, na inakuwa ya kuchanganya sana. Lakini kwa nini mchanganyiko? Kwa sababu watu wanajaribu kuwa wanahumanisti Wakristo. Humanismu ya Kikristo imekuwa ikikosoolewa mara nyingi kwa kubana na ugumu wa kuifafanua. Sababu imekuwa hivyo ya kuchanganya ni kwamba watu wanataka kuamini Mungu lakini pia waamini wao wenyewe na kwamba dunia inazunguka wao.

Katika Warumi, tunasoma, “For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet. And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient; Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them” (Romans 1:18-32).

Basi ni jinsi gani mtu anaweza kuwa mwanahumanisti na kuamini Mungu? Hapa ndipo tunagusa kidogo nyumbani. Aina hii ya mwanahumanisti anaamini Mungu anamtaka afurahie. Anaamini katika Mungu Muumba lakini hakubaliani kwamba lazima amtumikie Kwa uhalisia. Hapendi Mungu wa kweli bali, akifikiri kwake, ameunda mungu wa kubuni ambao hayupo. Hii inampa nafasi ya kuishi kwa ajili yake mwenyewe na furaha yake mwenyewe. Mtu wa aina hii atazungumza kuhusu Mungu, ataenda kanisani, ataimba nyimbo, na kusali. Hata hivyo, atatafuta binadamu pekee kwa mahitaji yake yote. Akiona mgonjwa, atamuita daktari. Akihitaji pesa, ataenda kwa benki. Ikiwa haja ni mapumziko kutoka kwa uhalisia, atachukua likizo au ukimya. Anaishi maisha kwa ajili ya furaha yake mwenyewe na kisha anamsifu Mungu ingawa hakumtazama Mungu kwa mahitaji yake. Watu hawa wategemea wenyewe. Wana ujasiri ndani yao.

Hapa kuna mfano: Mchrstiani anapanda bustani na kuijali kila siku. Anazimwagia na kuifugasha kinzani na kukata magomea. Mwishowe, mimea yake inaanza kuzaa matunda, matunda mazuri. Anamshukuru Mungu kwa mavuno mengi. Jirani yake, mwanahumanisti asiyeamini, pia alipanda bustani. Pia yeye alitoka kila siku na kuizimwagia, kukata, kuondoa magomea, na kuifugasha. Pia alipata mavuno mengi. Mtu huyu, hata hivyo, alijivunia yote aliyoyafikia. Wote wawili walifanya mambo sawa na walipata matokeo yanayofanana. Mmoja alimpa Mungu sifa, na mmoja alimpa sifa yeye mwenyewe. Atasema alifanya kitu kile kile bila Mungu kama jirani yake alivyofanya kwa msaada wa Mungu. Wakristo wanajua kwamba yeye anakosea na kwamba kwa kweli alihitaji Mungu kukua bustani yake.

Wakati jambo linatokea ambalo linahitaji uingiliaji wa kimungu, mwanahumanisti Mkristo anasali na kuwaomba wengine waombe. Hata hivyo, hakubali kuwa Mungu atawa jibu maombi yao na mara moja anaanza kufanya kazi ili kutatua tatizo la kwake kwa mantiki ya kibinadamu pekee. Kisha, ikiwa tatizo litatatuliwa, anamsifu Mungu kwa hilo. Aina hii ya humanismu imechanganya dunia ya kisasa. Imesababisha wasioamini kudharau imani ya Kikristo na kuitaja kuwa dini ya uongo isiyo na nguvu.

Mkristo hasemi kwa mantiki ya binadamu. Mkristo anaamini kuwa Mungu wa mbinguni ndiye sababu ya kila kitu. “For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him” (Colossians 1:16). Sisi ni kitu bure bila Yeye, na bila Yeye, hatuwezi kufanya chochote. Ukristo ni kinyume kabisa cha humanismu. Wakati Mkristo anafanya kitu cha kimazingira, kitu ambacho mwanahumanisti au mwanaasi hawezi kufanya, basi tunakuwa na kitu kitakachowachanganya wenye busara.

Wakati jirani anaona Mkristo akimpenda maadui wake, kumsamehe yule aliyemdhuru, na kufanya mambo ambayo yeye hawezi kufanya, basi anaanza kutafakari wapi nguvu za kufanya mambo haya ilitoka. Hii basi inamwelekeza kwa Baba. Wakati hakuna kitu cha kimazingira tunachofanya, yupo kwenye mchanganyiko.

Je, Kuhusu Sisi?

Ninaogopa kuwa tunapigwa na mtego huu wa ‘Humanismu wa Kikristo.’ Tunazungumza kwa maneno; tunasema tunaamini Mungu. Tunaenda kanisani, tunaimba nyimbo, na tunasali. Hata hivyo, kwa muonekano wa nje, tunamtegemea sisi wenyewe. Kwa sababu tumejikita maisha yetu kuzunguka sisi wenyewe na ustawi wetu, Mungu wa mbinguni hatusikii. Maombi yetu hayajibiwi, na muda wetu kwa magoti ni vita kwa vyema. Tunapata kuzunguka mfumo kwa sababu hivyo ndivyo tulivyofundishwa, lakini imani yetu ipo kwenye mantiki ya binadamu.

Inaweza kuwa ngumu sana kumwomba Bwana wakati unaishi katika jamii ya uhumanisti. Jamii ambayo imebobea katika kutafuta uhuru na furaha. Polepole, kanisa linakubali njia za dunia hii.

Kiongozi mmoja wa dini kutoka China alikuwa akitembelea makanisa nchini Amerika. Kabla ya kuondoka kurudi China, aliulizwa kilichomshangaza zaidi kuhusu makanisa nchini Amerika. Alijibu, “Nashangazwa na kile walichokamilisha bila Mungu.”

Tungefanya vyema kupunguza ufafanuzi wa kisasa wa humanismu. Mwanahumanisti kwa kiburi anakanusha kuwa kuna Mungu anapojibua nguvu na uwezo wake mwenyewe. Anatangaza mafanikio makubwa ya mwanadamu na kutesa Mkristo mnyenyekevu.

Mkristo anajinyima, anachukua msalaba wake, na kumfuata Mwalimu wake. Mkristo hatafikiri kitu juu yake mwenyewe au uwezo wa mwanadamu, akikiri kwa ujasiri kwamba yeye ni unga tu na atarudi kwa unga huo kwa haraka. Mkristo anatafuta mema kwa wengine na kumtumaini Mungu kwa mahitaji yake yote ya kila siku na mambo yake ya wazito.

Wakristo wanaamini wao ni watumishi tu kwa bwana wao. Wanachukiwa na dunia na walaaniwa na wengi, wakakataa. “If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you. (John 15:18)” Kwakeo, maisha haya sio kutafuta furaha. Mambo ya dunia hayawezi hata kuwavutia. Furaha na amani yao inatokana tu na kumtumikia bwana wao, kwa kumfurahisha Baba yao wa Mbingu. Kwa dunia, wao ni wa ajabu. Wachekeshaji. Kwa Mungu, wao ni watoto wake wapendwa.

Mungu bado anatafuta watu leo ambao watamuweka imani yao kwa Yeye. Anatafuta kote duniani mtu, mahali fulani, ambaye ataweka kando mantiki ya binadamu na busara ya kawaida na kutii sauti kutoka mbinguni. Mungu anataka wanaume wenye imani watakayetembea katika kimazingira, kama Abrahamu, Musa, Daudi, na maelfu ya waumini waliomfuata. Mtu atakayejinyima na dunia hii na kumfuata Mwokozi.

Wakati maisha haya yatakapokwisha, wanahumanisti, iwe wanasema wanaamini Mungu au la, watapotea. Na Wakristo wataendelea kuishi milele kwa utukufu.

Mwanahumanisti? Mkristo? Mwanahumanisti Mkristo? Wewe ni yupi?
